text:
Nikita Kucherov is playing out the last year of his contract and has said he won't be back in Tampa. He asked for a trade in late October; general manager Julien BriseBois said the Lightning have no intention of making one. On Sunday his line was benched in the third period of a 6-2 loss to Buffalo, and the cameras caught him on the bench with his gloves off, arms crossed. So the reigning Hart Trophy winner faces the defending Stanley Cup champions on national TV with everyone watching his body language as much as his hands.

The Lightning have reasons beyond Kucherov to feel thin. Brandon Hagel, 24 points in 20 games, is on injured reserve, and Conor Geekie had shoulder surgery and is out four to five months. Jake Guentzel has moved onto Hagel's spot with Anthony Cirelli and Kucherov, and Brayden Point is up to 18:43 a night. John Carlson, a summer arrival, has ten points in his last five games. The process is still good: Tampa takes 56% of the five-on-five expected goals, the quality of chances each side gets. Andrei Vasilevskiy is only +2.1 goals saved above expected after a +23.2 season, and that gap is most of the difference between a good team and a scary one.

Carolina looks like a team that never left June. The Hurricanes have points in seven straight (6-0-1) with 62% of the expected goals in that run on top of a 59% share at five on five for the season. The results are running a little ahead of even that, with finishing worth 6.0 extra goals and goaltending 7.4. Pyotr Kochetkov (+8.6) starts. Nikolaj Ehlers is out, so Taylor Hall, honored last week for 1,000 games, has moved up beside Logan Stankoven and Jackson Blake, the line that drove last spring's run. Stankoven has 13 points in ten games.

Our numbers lean Carolina on chances, 3.27 expected goals to 2.85. The Lightning are still 96% to make the playoffs. The nights are getting longer, though, and the conversation around Kucherov is not getting quieter.
headline: Kucherov, arms crossed, meets the champions
